title: Applications of derivatives in business and economics
competency: Use marginal cost, revenue and profit to find the best level.

keywords.def: P′(x): the extra profit from one more unit.
Money taken in: number sold × price.

en.text: Marginal cost, revenue and profit are the derivatives C′(x), R′(x), P′(x). Profit P = R − C, and revenue R = (number sold) × (price). The best level is where the marginal function is 0; a sign change from + to − confirms a maximum.

am.text: የህዳግ ወጪ፣ ገቢና ትርፍ C′(x), R′(x), P′(x) ናቸው። ትርፍ P = R − C፤ ገቢ = ብዛት × ዋጋ። ምርጡ ደረጃ የህዳግ ፋንክሽኑ 0 የሆነበት ነው።

screens.title: Selling more, earning less?
screens.ask: The price is P = 6 − x/2 birr for x items. Revenue is R = x(6 − x/2). Selling more items always gives more revenue?
screens.after:
R = x(6 − x/2) = 6x − x²/2.
More items means a lower price per item.
R′ = 6 − x = 0 at x = 6, so R(6) = 36 − 18 = 18 birr is the peak.
After x = 6 the price drop costs more than the extra sales bring: R falls.

screens.title: Marginal functions
paras: Marginal cost C′(x), marginal revenue R′(x), marginal profit P′(x).
screens.note: Set the marginal function to 0, then check the sign change.

screens.title: The marginal functions
items: Marginal cost: about the extra cost of one more unit.
Marginal revenue: about the extra money from one more unit sold.
Marginal profit: about the extra profit from one more unit.
Revenue is the number sold times the price of each.
A possible best level. P′ going + to − confirms a maximum.

screens.title: Find the best price
screens.ask: Theatre: 1000 people at 26 birr; each 1 birr off brings 50 more; each spends 4 birr on snacks. x = birr off the price.
screens.note: The peak is at x = 5: a 21 birr ticket.

screens.title: Key words
defs: P′(x): the extra profit from one more unit.
Money taken in: number sold × price.

screens.ask: Optimal sales volume: profit P(x) = x − 0.00001x² birr. Profit is largest when x = ___ units
screens.why:
Marginal profit: P′(x) = 1 − 0.00002x.
Set P′(x) = 0: 0.00002x = 1.
x = 1 ÷ 0.00002 = 50 000.
Check: P′ > 0 before 50 000 and < 0 after (+ to −), so it is a maximum.
Answer: 50 000 units.

screens.ask: Maximum profit: P(x) = x − 0.00001x². At x = 50 000 the profit is ___ birr

screens.title: Theatre ticket price
steps: R′ goes + to −: maximum. Ticket 26 − 5 = 21 birr.

screens.ask: Profit growing with time: R(x) = 1000x − x², C(x) = 3000 + 20x, x homes. Adding 10 homes a day at x = 400, the profit grows ___ birr per day
screens.why:
Chain rule: dR/dt = R′(x) × dx/dt, and the same for C.
R′(x) = 1000 − 2x = 1000 − 800 = 200 at x = 400.
dR/dt = 200 × 10 = 2000 birr per day.
C′(x) = 20, so dC/dt = 20 × 10 = 200 birr per day.
dP/dt = 2000 − 200 = 1800 birr per day.

screens.title: Profit P and marginal profit P′
screens.ask: Exercise 2.19: P(x) = x³ − 74x² + 40x − 27 490. Move x and compare P with P′.
screens.note: From x ≈ 49 on, P′ > 0: the profit is rising. But P stays negative until about x = 78.

screens.text: True or false? A positive marginal profit means the total profit is positive.
screens.why:
P′ tells how profit is changing, not how big it is.
At x = 50: P′(50) = 140 > 0.
But P(50) = 97 010 − 182 500 = −85 490: a loss.
The loss is shrinking, but it is still a loss. False.

screens.ask: Maximum revenue from a demand line: price p = 40 − 2x birr for x items. Revenue is largest at x = ___
screens.why:
Revenue = number sold × price: R = x(40 − 2x) = 40x − 2x².
R′(x) = 40 − 4x.
R′ = 0 gives x = 10.
R′ goes + to −, so it is a maximum: R(10) = 400 − 200 = 200 birr.
Trap: setting the price 40 − 2x = 0 gives x = 20, where revenue is 0.

items.text: Total profit: C(x) = 62x² + 27 500 and R(x) = x³ − 12x² + 40x + 10. Find P(x) = R(x) − C(x).
items.why:
P = (x³ − 12x² + 40x + 10) − (62x² + 27 500).
Subtract every term of C: −12x² − 62x² = −74x².
Constants: 10 − 27 500 = −27 490.
P(x) = x³ − 74x² + 40x − 27 490.
Trap: + 27 490 forgets to subtract the 27 500.

items.ask: Total profit at x = 50 for the same R and C: P(50) = ___

items.text: Marginal cost and marginal revenue at x = 50 (same C and R). Pick C′(50) and R′(50).

test.ask: Best level of output: P(x) = 40x − x². Profit is largest at x = ___
test.why:
P′(x) = 40 − 2x.
P′ = 0 gives x = 20.
P′ goes + to − at 20: a maximum.
Answer: x = 20.

test.ask: Maximum revenue: R(x) = 8x − 0.5x². The largest revenue is ___
test.why:
R′(x) = 8 − x = 0 gives x = 8.
R′ goes + to −: a maximum.
R(8) = 64 − 0.5(64) = 64 − 32 = 32.
Trap: 8 is the best x, not the revenue.

test.text: Profit, revenue and cost: profit P(x) equals
test.why:
Profit is the money taken in minus the money spent.
Money in = revenue R(x). Money spent = cost C(x).
So P(x) = R(x) − C(x).
C − R would be the loss; R′ is marginal revenue.

Marginal cost is C′(x).
C′(x) = 0 + 6x (the fixed 500 gives 0).
C′(10) = 60.

test.ask: Maximum revenue from a demand line: price p = 100 − 4x. Revenue is largest at x = ___
test.why:
R = x × p = 100x − 4x².
R′ = 100 − 8x.
R′ = 0 gives x = 100/8 = 12.5.
R′ goes + to −: a maximum.

notes.text: Example 3 (p.119) says the sign "changes from negative to positive at x = 5"; its own chart shows + to −, which gives the maximum. The answer (21 birr) is correct.

screens.text: First derivative test: f′ changes from − to + at c. Then f(c) is a
screens.why:
f′ < 0 before c: the graph falls.
f′ > 0 after c: the graph rises.
Falling then rising makes a valley.
So f(c) is a relative minimum.
